system.name: Grafting
system.one_liner: A two-stage way to edit pretrained diffusion transformers (activation distillation, then lightweight finetuning) so new architectures can be studied under small compute budgets.

content.variant_note: five titled panels of unequal size, each tied by the caption to a paper section: cost contrast and procedure on the left, three sample galleries on the right
content.argues: New diffusion architectures can be materialised by editing a pretrained model cheaply, and the grafted hybrid, text-to-image and depth-to-width models keep high image quality.
content.subject: Grafting versus training from scratch, the two-stage grafting procedure, and sample galleries of grafted models.

summary: The paper introduces grafting, a way to edit pretrained diffusion transformers so that new architectures can be studied cheaply, in two stages: activation distillation of each new operator, then lightweight finetuning. Figure 1 is a five-panel overview. (a) contrasts training from scratch (money bag) with grafting (coin stack) using bar-and-diamond model glyphs; (b) shows the procedure with its two stages and limited-data cylinders; (c) is a 3 by 6 grid of class-conditional samples from six hybrid designs with FID chips; (e) shows samples from a depth-to-width model; (d) shows four prompts with their 2048 by 2048 text-to-image samples. Pale-blue title strips head each panel and the galleries sit edge to edge.
summary_zh: 论文提出嫁接（grafting）：激活蒸馏加轻量微调，把预训练扩散 Transformer 改成新架构。图1五块：(a) 从头训练对嫁接，(b) 两阶段流程，(c) 六种混合结构样图与 FID，(e) 深度换宽度，(d) 文生图。
notes: The pre-screen listed four kinds; scope-overview is dropped because the galleries are the paper's own results (cards that are the paper's offerings), and contribution-mosaic takes the paper-roadmap variant because the caption ties panels to Sec. 3 to 6. The reading of bars as existing operators and diamonds as new ones comes from the stage text, not from labels in the figure. The chips r=3 with down arrow, r=6 with up arrow and A.R are not explained here (the abstract mentions variable MLP expansion ratio).
